newsitem.title: UK: Rothschild to advise on UK student loan sale.
newsitem.headline: Rothschild to advise on UK student loan sale.

text.p: Investment bank N M Rothschild & Sons said on Tusday it has been appointed by Britain's Department of Education to advise it on the potential sale of part of its student loan portfolio.
The portfolio consists of around 1.3 million loans with a total value of some 2.0 billion stg and is currently administered by the Student Loans Company, whose work is also to be contracted out.

"We expect there to be considerable demand for the loan assets from the private sector and we anticipate a variety of structures may be proposed for the purchase, including securitisation," Charles Keay, an executive director at Rothschilds said.
He noted the portfolio is expected to grow considerably, which could lead to further such sales.
"We envisage that the portfolio will be enhanced to allow for risk transfer from the public to the private sector at a rate that will be attractive," Keay added.
In September, the government postponed plans to allow private sector banks to give student loans alongside the SLC, after failing to reach agreement with three potential lenders.
